events.title: Winter Storm Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory above 6000 feet, moderate snow expected. Total snow accumulations 2 to 8 inches, with up to 16 inches near Lassen Volcanic National Park. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph. For the Winter Storm Watch above 4000 feet, heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 and 2 feet above 5000 feet possible, with up to 3 feet at the highest peaks. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8 inches between 4000 feet to 5000 feet, with up to 12 inches at 5000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 50 mph. * WHERE...For the Winter Weather Advisory, Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50, Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park. For the Winter Storm Watch, elevations above 4000 feet in the Sierra Nevada and southern Cascades. * WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 10 PM PST Monday. For the Winter Storm Watch, from Tuesday evening through early Friday morning. * IMPACTS...Snow covered roads, travel delays, and chain controls possible this afternoon into Monday. The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning and evening commutes. Travel could be very difficult to impossible Tuesday night through early Friday morning. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches and significant reductions in visibilities. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet today, dropping to around 5000 to 6000 feet Monday. Heaviest snow is expected late tonight into Monday morning. Lull in activity expected on Tuesday, followed by a colder, stronger system by mid-week. Snow levels 3500-4500 feet Tuesday night, rising to around 4500-6000 feet Wednesday. Heaviest snow is expected Wednesday afternoon into the overnight hours, with snowfall rates 1-2+ inches per hour.

events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Heavy snow may impact the Wednesday morning commute. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions could impact the Wednesday morning and evening commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The heaviest snow is likely early Wednesday, around 1 AM to 8 AM PST, and will include Snowman Summit and Scott Mountain Summit. A break in the snow is possible late Wednesday afternoon and evening, ahead of additional light snow showers late Wednesday night.

weather.instruction:
Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep
you warmer than a single heavy coat. Cover exposed skin to reduce
your risk of frostbite or hypothermia. Gloves, a scarf, and a hat
will keep you from losing your body heat.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa Coastal Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 6:56PM CST until November 20 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to
midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk,
from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to
1 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best

weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 17 at 1:28AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to
1 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 10 and 18 inches above 4000 ft and winds gusting as high as 50 mph. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 8 inches below 4000 ft and winds gusting as high as 35 mph. * WHERE...The Winter Storm Warning is for areas above 4000 ft, including Snowman and Dead Horse Summits on highway 89, and Everitt Memorial Highway and the Old SKi Bowl. The Winter Weather Advisory includes the Interstate 5 Corridor between Black Butte Summit and Weed, and the cities of Mount Shasta City and McCloud. * WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on tree limbs may down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages.

location.region: South Central Siskiyou County

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and

weather.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 12:26PM PST until November 19 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
13 to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking
waves of 15 to 18 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to
4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.
weather.instruction:
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...North Bay Interior Valleys and San Francisco Bay Shoreline Counties. * WHEN...From 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:53 AM Wednesday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 8:51AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 2
feet expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet
above 8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...A portion of central California.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected in the Eastern Sierra. For elevations between 5,000 and 8,000 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 10 to 18 inches expected. For elevations between 8,000 and 9,500 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 18 to 36 inches expected. Locally higher totals expected above 9,500 feet. Winds could gust as high as 55 mph. * WHERE...Eastern Sierra Slopes. * WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening commutes. Strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and power lines. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Whiteout conditions are expected and will make travel treacherous and potentially life-threatening.

weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

dangerous surf conditions.

shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Flagler, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern Inland St. Johns, Southeast Coastal St. Johns, Southern Inland St. Johns and Western St. Johns. * WHEN...From 5 PM EST this afternoon through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur in the watch area through the end of the week. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small stream flooding for the coastal areas of northeast Florida. Total rainfall forecast through Friday night is around 3 to 8 inches with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches or more. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, SW Kenai Peninsula, NW Kenai Peninsula, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Power outages and tree damage are likely due to the ice. Travel could be nearly impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

weather.instruction:

vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 2:01AM CST until November 19 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or
pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except
those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable
to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of
Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, and NW Kenai Peninsula; heavy snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This product was updated to remove SW Kenai Peninsula and correct impact information in the bullet above. An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

location.region: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River; Lower Matanuska Valley; NW Kenai Peninsula; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 10 and 18 inches above 4000 ft and winds gusting as high as 50 mph. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 8 inches below 4000 ft and winds gusting as high as 35 mph. * WHERE...The Winter Storm Warning is for areas above 4000 ft, including Snowman and Dead Horse Summits on highway 89, and Everitt Memorial Highway and the Old SKi Bowl. The Winter Weather Advisory includes the Interstate 5 Corridor between Black Butte Summit and Weed, and the cities of Mount Shasta City and McCloud. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on tree limbs may down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages.

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 18 at 9:01AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 3 feet
expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet above
8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday
morning commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday morning. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Flash Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall are possible over the Plaskett and Timber burn areas. * WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur. For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including Los Burros Road. * WHEN...Through late tonight. * IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons. Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead to flash flooding and debris flows. - Some locations that may experience flash flooding include... Big Sur, Plaskett, and Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Eastern Clay, Eastern Putnam, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern Inland St. Johns, South Central Duval, Southeast Coastal St. Johns, Southern Inland St. Johns, Trout River, Western Clay, Western Duval, Western Putnam and Western St. Johns. * WHEN...Through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur in the watch area through the end of the week. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small stream flooding for the coastal areas of northeast Florida. Total rainfall forecast through Friday night is around 3 to 8 inches with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches or more. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at 1049 PM tonight, 1104 AM Thursday, and 1041 Thursday night.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 1:16PM CST until November 19 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1049 PM tonight, 1104 AM Thursday, and 1041 Thursday night.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.0 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 3.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.6 feet Sunday evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL

weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong

forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall over recent weeks has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. Additional heavy rainfall should cause the river to reach major flood stage Friday. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate flooding is occurring and Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 10.5 feet, Water covers many secondary roads near the river, limiting access to homes to boats or high terrain vehicles. Flooding of homes along secondary roads near the river becomes more significant. Water begins to encroach on State Road 46 near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 9.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 9.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 10.4 feet Sunday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

.Heavy rainfall over recent weeks has caused river levels on the St.

stage Friday.

flooding is occurring and Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

significant. Water begins to encroach on State Road 46 near Jungle
Road and Prevatt Road.

- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 9.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on snow is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam Gulch. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways. Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This includes the city of Seward. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. events.description: AVAREV The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S. Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center. BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED 08:55 PST Wed Nov 18 2026 The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA)) * WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger is anticipated in the backcountry from around sunset on Wednesday into early Friday morning. * WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass(Hwy 4) on the south, including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs exist. * WHEN...In effect from Wed 08:55 PST to Thu 05:00 PST. * IMPACTS...Significant snowfall may lead to widespread avalanche activity in the mountains. Large avalanches capable of burying or injuring people could occur in backcountry areas. * PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche conditions could occur in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain during HIGH avalanche danger is not recommended. Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org for more detailed information. Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored break points. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.instruction:

changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

The effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor exercise or strenuous activity. For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 3:43AM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 3:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 3:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.7 feet early Monday morning. events.title: Flash Flood Warning
events.description: FFWLOX The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... West Central Santa Barbara County in southwestern California... * Until 245 AM PST. * At 1244 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.75 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour, much of which may fall in 15 to 30 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash flooding. SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Vandenberg Space Force Base, Orcutt and Vandenberg Village.

location.region: Santa Barbara, CA

weather.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 12:44AM PST until November 19 at 2:45AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
FFWLOX

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Santa Barbara County in southwestern California...

* Until 245 AM PST.

* At 1244 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches
of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.75 to 1.5
inches in 1 hour, much of which may fall in 15 to 30 minutes. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Vandenberg Space Force Base, Orcutt and Vandenberg Village.
weather.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
weather.areaDesc: Santa Barbara, CA

events.title: Cold Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Cold conditions with temperatures as low as 33 to 36 degrees expected. * WHERE...The East Bay. * WHEN...From 1 AM to 8 AM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia for people and animals.

location.region: East Bay Interior Valleys; East Bay Hills

weather.headline: Cold Weather Advisory issued November 18 at 10:20PM PST until November 21 at 8:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Cold conditions with temperatures as low as 33 to 36 degrees
expected.

* WHERE...The East Bay.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 8 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
weather.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.
weather.areaDesc: East Bay Interior Valleys; East Bay Hills

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and rough surf. * WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 1:19AM EST until November 21 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flash Flood Watch
events.description: Between 3 to 6 inches of rain have fallen across the Santa Lucia Range impacting the Timber and Plaskett Fire Burn Scars over the last 24 hours. Expect additional rounds of scattered moderate to heavy rain impacting the Central Coast and Napa County through Thursday evening. * WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall continue to be possible over the Plaskett burn area and Timber burn area. * WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur. For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including Los Burros Road. * WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons. Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead to flash flooding and debris flows. - Some locations that may experience flash flooding include... Big Sur, Plaskett, and Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some

and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially

ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through
